reviewer: Codex, independent. Did not author v1 or v2 and did not read the concurrent reviewer.
summary: The v1-to-v2 honesty repair is closed and correctly attributes the full-width no-lock rule to this proposal rather than D-013. The candidate nevertheless fails at four blocking points: one governing-source pin is stale under its own mandatory review rule; the immutable archive member has no emitted/signed custody carrier and its determinism is assigned to an unrelated canonical-JSON dependency; the DR-103 fixture dependency names immutable corpus v1 even though both independent reviews rejected those bytes; and AT-7 reduces the row's required gate-compliance proof to presence of evidence references. Three additional interface/custody issues require repair. DR-120 and DR-103 remain OPEN; nothing is authorized.

blockers.title: The coordinator-decision governing-source digest is stale, which the artifact's own review rule makes a blocker
blockers.detail: The live register advanced through adopted D-103. The append preserves the negative authority boundaries relevant here, but v2's rule is categorical: 'Re-measure every recordedInputs digest. A mismatch is a blocker.' Its recordedInputs discipline also says every listed input was measured. Independent review cannot waive the artifact's explicit custody gate because the newly appended decision happens to be compatible.
blockers.minimumRepair: Issue a successor with the live coordinator digest, refresh the role/standing account to include the adopted D-103 fact where relevant, and remeasure every source again at dispatch.

blockers.title: OC-2 names an immutable archive but emits no archive bytes or digest carrier, and assigns archive reproducibility to canonical JSON
blockers.sourceObligation: File 02 C-3 requires 'immutable archive and full-tree path/type/mode/length/digest commitment, including entrypoint and required runtime/tool bytes'.
blockers.measurement: OC-2's emits field specifies only a per-platform TreeCommitment. S-3-EMIT lists manifest, per-platform tree, declarations, detached-signature binding point, and report, but no archive. The whole artifact has zero 'archiveDigest' fields and no manifestDigest/report join. Accepted schemas.v2's manifest TreeCommitment commits extracted entries, not archive bytes; its index has no archive digest; per-artifact archive digests appear only in the lock shape, while this artifact correctly says no lock is producible before DR-111.
blockers.secondDefect: CI-3 and ID-DEP-P1 say byte-identical archives ride component-schema ID-DEP-1. The cited ID-DEP-1 owns canonical JSON signing preimages for manifest/index and conditional lock serialization; it says nothing about archive ordering, metadata normalization, timestamps, ownership fields, or compression. Canonical JSON cannot make an archive reproducible.
blockers.impact: One of file 02's nine output members has a name but no exact-byte carrier. The signed offline payload and exact-byte-delivery claims therefore cannot join the verified archive to the committed tree, and the named dependency cannot ever repair that gap.
blockers.minimumRepair: Define a tool-neutral archive artifact and sha256-of-exact-bytes carrier, bind it into an accepted signed-custody surface (or name the precise schema-successor dependency), and state the deterministic archive profile/owner separately from canonical JSON. Keep concrete packager/tool choices deferred.

blockers.title: ID-DEP-P8 makes DR-103 closure ride on corpus v1 even though both independent reviews rejected those immutable bytes
subjectClaims: The governing-source role describes corpus v1 as AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW.
FG-4 says 'Its review is a separate SATISFIED-GRADE act.'
ID-DEP-P8 rides on 'Independent SATISFIED-GRADE review of component-manifest-fixture-corpus.v1'.
blockers.measurement: The immutable v1 bytes d81a4ef9... already have two independent REJECT verdicts: Claude 2 2bbdc392... (4 blockers, 4 SHOULD-FIX) and Codex 4509ee42... (9 blockers, 1 SHOULD-FIX). A successor draft exists at corpus v2 70248781..., itself CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED / DRAFT-AWAITING-SCHEMA-SUCCESSOR / binds NOTHING. Re-review cannot repair v1 bytes, so the named ride cannot reach acceptance as written.
blockers.whatIsNotWrong: The artifact repeatedly denies that citing v1 is an adapter run or SATISFIED evidence; that dispatched attack fails. The blocker is the opposite end of the dependency: v1 is still named as the future closure vehicle after it has conclusively failed review.
blockers.minimumRepair: Record both v1 REJECT verdicts and make ID-DEP-P8 ride on an independently accepted SATISFIED-grade successor corpus against the applicable accepted schema, plus later D-000 MF-6. Keep current corpus successors explicitly candidate-only and do not infer adapter execution from them.

blockers.title: AT-7 replaces the required gate-compliance proof with evidence-reference presence
blockers.sourceObligation: The live DR-120 acceptance cell requires fixtures proving 'gate compliance' across representative language closures; file 02 C-13 likewise requires acceptance tests for all relevant size/quality/performance gates.
blockers.subjectRule: AT-7 says the emission binds evidence paths and explicitly concludes: 'This class proves the binding points exist, not that numbers pass.' The word map repeats 'class only; numbers at D-006/DR-115/DR-118'.
blockers.impact: A path to evidence is not proof that the owning gate passed. The artifact may defer threshold values and measurement to their owners, but it cannot redefine compliance as reference presence while claiming every cell fragment is answered. Under this contract an adapter could satisfy AT-7 with a digest-bound failing result.
blockers.minimumRepair: Keep threshold ownership external, but require the conditional AT-7 execution to resolve each applicable owner-defined gate result, verify its exact evidence custody, and require a passing standing before reporting compliance. Until an owner supplies a gate or disposition, report blocked-on-ride rather than compliant.

shouldFix.title: The contract does not separate production adapter emission from hostile-fixture generation
shouldFix.detail: S-3-EMIT requires structurally valid schema output and forbids populating reserved points. FG-1 then says the same adapter MUST emit every nonconditional DR-103 fixture class, which includes duplicate identities, hostile paths, digest mismatches, reserved-field population, and other outputs the production adapter must refuse. AT-3 further permits either adapter production or refusal of an authored hostile fixture, so the interface has two incompatible accounts.
shouldFix.whyShouldFix: The fixtureGeneration container supplies test context, so this does not by itself authorize invalid release output; however, the DR-120 adapter interface cannot remain ambiguous about which normative mode emits adversarial bytes.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Define a separate test-only fixture generator/mutator that starts from a valid adapter emission, creates one controlled invalidity, and is impossible to invoke as production S-3-EMIT. State which classes are generated by valid adapter runs versus mutation/refusal harnesses.

shouldFix.title: Signed clean-install and offline tests are not conditioned on the open DR-112 ceremony they require
shouldFix.detail: AT-1 requires clean install from signed offline inputs and AT-5 requires no-network install with trust slots. ID-DEP-P3 correctly names signature-envelope ceremony as riding DR-112, but its consequence marks only OC-8 and AT-6 inactive and says ceremony fixtures are elsewhere. It never classifies the signature-validity arms of AT-1/AT-5. With roots, thresholds, revocation, expiry, and envelope validity open, a harness cannot decide that signed inputs are installable rather than typed-unavailable.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Split packaging-byte/offline-assembly checks from trust-validity/install-success checks. Put the latter explicitly behind DR-112/DR-110 using the same scoped-disposition symmetry rule used by AT-6.

shouldFix.title: The conformance report is not joined to exact subject/run custody and permits ungoverned self-exemption
shouldFix.detail: The report subject is only {stableId, version, platform}; it carries no manifest digest, provenance/scope discriminator, adapter version/digest, source-tree/tool-closure input pins, or run identity. outputContractMembers.digestOrRef is optional and may be either a sha256 or a path rather than an exact {path, sha256} join. fixtureClassCoverage permits not-applicable and blocked-on-ride, with an optional ride and no closed eligibility rule. A report can therefore be replayed across different bytes of the same release tuple or self-mark required classes inapplicable without a named owner disposition.
shouldFix.whyShouldFix: CI-1 requires those inputs to be pinned and DR-G15 may retain additional out-of-band custody, so this is narrower than the missing OC-2 carrier. The promised single report shape should nevertheless carry the pins and closed exemption rules needed to audit its own claims.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Add exact manifest/tree-or-archive/report/input joins and adapter identity/version digest; require {path, sha256} where evidence is referenced; enumerate the only lawful not-applicable/blocked rides and require the owning dependency/disposition for each.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed: Choosing a concrete packager, toolchain, CLI, CI vendor, or command line. The artifact names examples only to deny selection and keeps the choice in the implementation reservation.

Treating the hand-authored DR-103 corpus as an adapter run or SATISFIED by citation. FG-3/FG-4 and whatThisDoesNotDo deny both; CPCV2-B3 concerns the stale future ride, not a positive acceptance claim.
Attributing the full-width no-lock rule to D-013/schemas.v2. The v2 repair correctly separates the constrained-request holding from this proposal's widening.
A silent v1-to-v2 path outside the repair roster. Recursive comparison found none.

A positive SATISFIED, QUALIFIED, DEMONSTRATED, or implementation-authorization claim. Hits are denials, review attacks, measured external row standings, or opaque-token exclusions. status remains CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED / DO-NOT-SEAL / binds NOTHING.
A DR-120 row or file-02 carried-text mismatch. Both are byte-exact.
verdictBasis: 4 blockers, 3 SHOULD-FIX, 0 advisories. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
verdictStatement: REJECT. The targeted ID-DEP-P2 repair is correct and the closed delta is honest, but the candidate cannot serve as DR-120's accepted design contract while a mandatory source pin fails, an enumerated archive output has no custody carrier, the fixture closure ride points to already rejected immutable bytes, and gate compliance is defined as reference presence rather than pass. The three narrower interface/custody defects also remain. This verdict does not mark DR-120 or DR-103 SATISFIED and authorizes no implementation.

authorityOfThisVerdict.note: Independent measurement only. Both rows remain OPEN; coordinator disposition is separate.

coordinatorNote: The v2 honesty repair should be retained: it correctly stops lending D-013's acceptance to the full-width lock rule. A successor needs more than a pin refresh, however. It must supply an exact immutable-archive custody carrier and correct archive determinism owner, point fixture closure at an accepted successor rather than dual-REJECT v1, and restore actual owner-gate pass semantics to AT-7. It should also split hostile fixture generation from production emission, condition signed install tests on DR-112, and make the conformance report exact-byte auditable. DR-120 and DR-103 remain OPEN.
